comments.text:
Let's face it people, it's just not sustainable now.   It will be the ultra-rich and the poor. The middle class has slipped away.
Honestly, people are exhausted by a rat race where hard work no longer reliably leads to getting ahead. They're being nickel-and-dimed to death by fees, over-taxed, and squeezed by asset-stripping costs that price them out of homeownership while rents climb to unsustainable levels. 

It's a rational response to a system that feels increasingly rigged against the average person.  We're witnessing a quiet revolt against these conditions. The middle class has been hollowed out, leaving a growing divide between the ultra-wealthy and everyone else. Recent reports from Bank of America highlight a troubling trend: more people are now using credit cards not for discretionary spending, but as a basic budgeting tool to survive month to month—financing groceries, utilities, and everyday essentials. That's not what credit was meant for, and it's a clear sign of deeper strain.  

Wages have stagnated for years while inflation has eroded purchasing power. In this high-cost environment....so "working harder" at traditional jobs often isn't enough. Navigating stagnant wages requires aggressive income optimization—side hustles, skill upgrades, with a very disciplined expense management scheme. But even that only goes so far when the fundamentals (housing, healthcare, education) keep outpacing income growth.
